option.approach: Separate order completeness from quasitrace-metric convergence. Determine whether the proposed constant-gap sequence could have a supremum without converging in that metric, explaining why the metric argument would not decide the question.

options.approach: Audit the precise completeness theorem needed, distinguishing projection suprema, suprema of commuting sequences, and suprema of arbitrary increasing self-adjoint sequences. Locate the exact unsupported implication in the previous argument.

options.counterfactual: The quasitrace axioms alone rule out bounded positive partial sums whose individual summands all have the same strictly positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Seek a quantitative exhaustion inequality bounding the number of positive summands with quasitrace at least a fixed threshold when their sum is bounded by 1. Such an inequality would prove that the set in the question is empty without using the AW* assumptions.

options.counterfactual: An increasing positive sequence with constant positive quasitrace increments can exist in a finite AW*-factor and can lack a least upper bound, so the set in the question is nonempty.
options.approach: Start from one witness and investigate transformations that enlarge its increment value while preserving boundedness and the absence of a least upper bound. Combine these with scaling to determine the endpoint of the resulting initial interval.
